Patch Notes

4.4.0 — The Code Testing Guild: an executable code-verification gauntlet

This release adds GUILD-040, the Code Testing Guild, as an additive, executable code-verification layer. It does not remove, disable, or replace any existing testing behavior — the full existing test suite and every prior Standing Operation continue to run unchanged. What is new is that the operating system can now classify a code change's risk, enforce a criticality-weighted test gauntlet, and produce independently verifiable release evidence, all deterministically in code rather than by prompt instruction alone.

What is new

  • A deterministic criticality classifier (lpos_engine.code_testing.classify) that

maps change signals to LIGHT, STANDARD, HIGH, or CRITICAL. It is total: unknown or absent signals default to STANDARD and it never raises. Destructive operations, secrets, financial movement, irreversible migrations, and production infrastructure force CRITICAL; auth, permissions, customer data, public APIs, migrations, concurrency, and a broad blast radius force at least HIGH.

  • The Code Testing Gauntlet Standard as data and gates: the cumulative tier →

required-gate table, plus a release-decision evaluator that REJECTS when a required command did not run, when a gate failed or is flaky, or when only a green unit suite is offered for STANDARD or above.

  • The Need-to-Change Gate: a production change requires a reproduction, a demonstrated

missing behavior, or an objective-constraint proof; absent all three the correct successful result is NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED.

  • Release evidence packets with a test-independence rule that mirrors Sentinel: a

producer cannot audit its own release, so the independent reviewer may not be the implementer.

  • A dependency-free testing-manifest loader that reads repository-native commands and

never invents a build, test, lint, or type-check command.

  • 12 specialists (SPECIALIST-034 through SPECIALIST-045) in the new Code Testing

guild, from the Code Test Director to the Release Verification Auditor.

  • Three Standing Operations: SO-027 Code Test Gauntlet (event-driven, per code

change), SO-028 Test Suite Health Review (weekly), and SO-029 Critical Path Hardening (event-driven, before a HIGH or CRITICAL release).

  • Four Hermes skills: code-test-gauntlet, code-criticality-classifier,

acceptance-spec-reviewer, and test-evidence-auditor.

  • **The code_testing engine module** and a small CLI:

python -m lpos_engine.code_testing classify|gauntlet.

Counts

  • Specialists 33 → 45, Standing Operations 26 → 29, benchmarks 55 → 70, schemas

unchanged at 20.

Additive and preserving

The Code Testing Guild is additive. Existing testing behavior is preserved: nothing in the prior release is retired, and the new gauntlet sits alongside — not in place of — the current tests and Standing Operations. See Code testing.

Seeing that the code is tested

  • The Test Coverage Map (tools/build_test_report.py → dist/test-coverage.html): a

self-contained page listing every source module, whether it is under test, its measured line coverage, and its gauntlet tier. Rows sort by coverage so gaps surface at the top — it is honest by design (CLI entry modules that pytest does not import show as low, rather than being hidden). Coverage numbers come from running the full suite under coverage.py; the page degrades to a static module↔test map when coverage.py is absent, keeping the OS itself dependency-free.

Writing quality

  • **anti-slop-editor 1.0.1** migrated in from the approved, verified Hermes skill: a

named-pattern de-AI editing pass that uses minimum-effective edits to preserve Dan, Chip, and LPOS voice, enforces deterministic lint behavior, and explicitly refuses to guess whether text was AI-authored. CS-001, zero em dashes, and independent review remain authoritative. Preserved alongside it (unchanged): quality-router 2.2.0 prose routing, lpos-core 3.1.0 writing rules, and the voice/editor overlays — migrated explicitly rather than by editing a signed release in place.
